acceptance: `pr-arm WAIT=<n>` survives a rate-limit response and resumes after the reset when it falls inside the wait (test with a stubbed API).
`pr-open` reports the reset time when it refuses for a rate limit.
context: Filed 2026-11-12 from the scale-factor follow-up and TPC-DI generator work of 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12: identified during that work and not addressed.
description:
## Problem
Several agent sessions share one GitHub user's 5,000 requests per hour. On 2026-11-12 the limit was exhausted twice in an hour:
- `make pr-open` refused with 'the local review is unavailable: the open pull request for this branch could not be read ... API rate limit exceeded' and pushed nothing, although the review had not run.
- `make pr-arm WAIT=60` exited with 'live state could not be verified: cannot read tracker index ... API rate limit exceeded' 24 minutes into its wait, although the reset was minutes away. A separate run ended on a GitHub HTTP 503 after three attempts.
The caller had to poll `gh api rate_limit` by hand and re-run. The messages do not name the reset time.

## Change
Treat a rate-limit response as a wait: read the reset time, say it, and resume, at least inside `pr-arm WAIT`. Reduce request volume in the polling paths (conditional requests or longer intervals), and consider a shared budget across sessions.

## Guardrails
- Never treat an unreadable state as a pass; waiting is the only relaxation.
- Keep the wait bounded by `WAIT`.
